newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says sets 10-year bonds offer Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says sets 10-year bonds offer Sept 24.

text.p: The Philippine Bureau of Treasury said on Thursday it will hold an auction for 10-year fixed rate treasury bonds on September 24.
"This will be the first time that we are issuing 10-year bonds to the public," treasury director Roberto Dispo said.
Some two billion pesos worth of 10-year fixed rate treasury bonds will be auctioned on September 24 and there will be regular 10-year bond auctions every three months after that, Dispo added.
The government is trying to lead the way in deepening the domestic financial market by diversifying government securities, as well as lengthening the maturity of its domestic debt.
The Philippines used to issues only one-year treasury bills. It introduced two year fixed-rate treasury notes in 1994 and five-year fixed rate T-notes in 1995.
Early this year, the government also started issuing seven-year treasury notes.
Dispo said the coupon rate on the 10-year bonds will be based on the rates submitted by the majority.

"Using the Dutch auction method, the 10-year fixed rate treasury bill coupon rate shall be based on the stop-out rate set by the auction committee rounded down to the nearest 1/8 of one percent," the treasury department said.
